overview.title: 📖 Overview: Finishing the Eighteen Decrees
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 17a–17b
overview.hebrewSource: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם הָיָה קָשֶׁה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּיּוֹם שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בּוֹ הָעֵגֶל
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens with Rabbi Akiva's careful correction of the ox-goad impurity ruling, then completes the tally of the eighteen decrees: the tense story of how the dispute over harvesting grapes for the press led Beit Shammai's students to physically outvote Beit Hillel's, several more decrees protecting teruma and separating Jews from gentile culture, and finally a new mishna opening a fresh topic — whether one may begin, on Friday, a process that will only finish on its own once Shabbat has started.

slides.title: 🐫 Rabbi Akiva's Correction: When Does an Object Transmit Corpse-Impurity?
slides.subtitle: Untangling a 'garbled halakha,' per Rabbi Tarfon's protest

nodes.content: ❓ Rabbi Tarfon: the common version of the ox-goad ruling is garbled — 'I will bury my sons if this is not so!'
🔧 Rabbi Akiva: I will correct it so that the Sages' words all hold together

columns.label: To the carrier
columns.content: Impure only if the object is at least the width of an ox-goad

columns.label: To the object itself
columns.content: Becomes impure at any size at all, acting as its own 'tent' over the corpse

columns.label: To others it touches
columns.content: Transmits impurity onward only if it has an opening a handbreadth wide

nodes.content: 📏 Rabbi Yannai adds: this 'ox-goad' is narrow in width but a handbreadth in circumference — the Sages decreed on its circumference precisely because its width alone would not have qualified

slides.title: ⚔️ A Sword in the Study Hall
slides.subtitle: Grapes, olives, and the day Beit Shammai outvoted Beit Hillel
slides.hebrewSource: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם הָיָה קָשֶׁה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּיּוֹם שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בּוֹ הָעֵגֶל
slides.label: The confrontation:
slides.text: Hillel and Shammai disputed whether grapes gathered for the press become susceptible to impurity through their own seeping juice. Hillel challenged: 'If so, why do we gather grapes in purity but not olives?' Shammai retorted: 'If you provoke me, I will decree impurity on the olive harvest too!' The dispute grew so heated that they stuck a sword in the study hall doorway, declaring that whoever wished to enter could, but no one could leave. That day Hillel sat bowed before Shammai like one of the students — a day the Gemara calls 'as difficult for Israel as the day the Golden Calf was made.' Even so, the people did not accept the decree from Hillel and Shammai themselves; only when their own students later reissued it was it accepted.

slides.title: 🍇 Why Does Gathering Grapes Cause Susceptibility to Impurity?
slides.subtitle: Three attempts to explain the decree
rows: Lest one gather the grapes in impure baskets, whose impurity would confer deliberate-liquid status on the seeping juice — though this only works for one view of how impure vessels affect liquids
Lest one gather into sealed, pitched baskets, where the juice pools instead of spilling out — making its presence there effectively wanted
Juice is squeezed out willfully when separating clusters stuck together — just as a person sometimes squeezes a cluster on purpose, to test whether the grapes are ripe enough to harvest

slides.title: 📋 More of the Eighteen — Growths, a Dark Road, and Gentile Goods
slides.subtitle: Completing the list of decrees from Ḥananya's attic

steps.content: 1️⃣ Produce grown from planted teruma is itself teruma — lest a priest keep impure teruma to plant later, forget it is impure, and come to eat from what grows
2️⃣ One caught by nightfall on the road, Shabbat eve, with a purse must hand it to a gentile companion rather than carry it in Torah-permitted increments of under four cubits at a time
3️⃣ A single chained decree covers gentile bread and oil (because of their wine), their wine (because it leads to marrying their daughters), and their daughters (because of idolatry)
4️⃣ The chain's final link: even a gentile infant is treated as one who transmits impurity like a full zav — to keep Jewish children from growing overly familiar with gentile children

slides.title: 🕰️ New Mishna: Starting on Friday, Finishing on Shabbat
slides.subtitle: May a process begun before Shabbat simply continue on its own?

lines.speaker: Beit Shammai
lines.text: One may only begin soaking dye or ink, drying flax in the oven, or dyeing wool on Shabbat eve if enough daylight remains for the process to be substantially finished before Shabbat starts.

lines.speaker: Beit Hillel
lines.text: Permit starting these processes even without enough daylight left — they may simply continue on their own once Shabbat has begun.

lines.speaker: Same principle
lines.text: Beit Shammai: traps for animals, birds, or fish must be set only with enough daylight to catch something before Shabbat; selling to a gentile or giving him hides or laundry likewise needs enough time for him to finish or reach a nearby place.

lines.speaker: Same principle
lines.text: Beit Hillel permits all of these regardless of how much daylight remains.

summary.principle: The eighteen decrees close with the Gemara's fullest picture yet of how contested they were — a dispute so sharp it required a sword in the doorway — and open a new question that will run through the coming dafim: how much of a Shabbat-bound process may be set in motion just before Shabbat begins.

flowSteps.content: 🐫 Rabbi Akiva sorts out exactly when a movable object transmits corpse-impurity, and to whom
⚔️ The grape-harvest dispute turns so heated that Beit Shammai's students outvote Beit Hillel's by force of numbers

columns.content: 📋 Teruma's growths, a purse on a dark road, and gentile bread, wine, and daughters round out the eighteen
🕰️ A new mishna asks how much daylight a Friday process needs before it may continue into Shabbat

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Even hard-won decrees only took hold once the next generation's students, not the original masters, reissued them

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Akiva's correction, at what minimum size does a movable object transmit corpse-impurity to the person carrying it?
o: Any size at all
At least the width of an ox-goad
Only if it has an opening a handbreadth wide
Only if it directly touches the corpse
quiz.e: Rabbi Akiva ruled that an object transmits impurity to the person carrying it once it reaches at least the width of an ox-goad; it becomes impure itself at any size, but transmits to others only with a handbreadth opening.

quiz.q: What triggered the sharp confrontation between Hillel and Shammai that led to a sword being placed in the study hall doorway?
o: A dispute over the calendar
Hillel's challenge about why grapes are gathered in purity but not olives, and Shammai's threat to decree impurity on olives too
A disagreement over the laws of divorce
An argument about who should be Nasi
quiz.e: Hillel pressed Shammai on the inconsistency between grape and olive harvesting; Shammai's threatened response escalated the dispute to the point that a sword was set in the doorway and a vote was forced.

quiz.q: According to Rava, why does the juice that seeps from grape clusters render them susceptible to impurity?
o: Because grape juice is always considered a liquid placed willfully
Because it is squeezed out willfully when separating clusters stuck together, just as one might deliberately squeeze a cluster to test ripeness
Because grapes are inherently more susceptible than other fruit
Because the baskets used are always impure
quiz.e: Rava explained that people sometimes squeeze grape clusters on purpose (e.g. to check ripeness), which is enough to render the resulting juice a liquid placed willfully, making the fruit susceptible to impurity.

quiz.q: Why did the Sages decree that produce grown from planted teruma remains teruma?
o: To increase the amount of teruma given to priests
Lest a priest keep impure teruma to plant later, forget that it is impure, and come to eat from what grows
Because planted teruma automatically becomes holier
To prevent farmers from ever planting teruma seeds
quiz.e: Rava explained the concern is a priest holding impure teruma who might plant it rather than destroy it, later forgetting its impure status and eating the produce that grows from it.

quiz.q: According to the new mishna, how do Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel differ regarding starting a process on Friday (like soaking dye or setting animal traps) that will only finish on Shabbat?
o: Beit Shammai forbids starting any such process at all
Beit Shammai requires enough daylight left for it to be substantially finished before Shabbat begins; Beit Hillel permits starting it regardless
Beit Hillel forbids it while Beit Shammai permits it freely
Both schools agree such processes are always forbidden
quiz.e: Beit Shammai requires sufficient time before Shabbat for the process (soaking, drying, trapping, etc.) to be substantially completed; Beit Hillel permits starting it even without that much daylight remaining.
